answer: Each identity is verified by a Wesolowski VDF: repeated modular squarings form a dependency chain, so the next step cannot begin before the previous one finishes. GPUs may run separate chains concurrently, but cannot divide one chain to remove its sequential delay; creating many clones therefore requires many independently completed proofs. This time cost is a bottleneck, not identity uniqueness, and its burden can be described as a terrace across each dune to a valid vertex.
